class.name: GDScriptTrait
class.brief_description: A reusable bundle of members that classes can include with the [code]uses[/code] keyword.
class.description:
A trait is declared with the [code]trait[/code] keyword and holds any member a class can hold, except inner classes. Classes bring a trait's members into themselves with [code]uses[/code]. [codeblock] trait Damageable: const MAX_HEALTH := 100 var health: int = MAX_HEALTH
func take_damage(amount: int) -> void: health -= amount
func is_dead() -> bool: return health <= 0
class Player extends Node: uses Damageable
# The class's own version takes precedence over the trait's. func take_damage(amount: int) -> void: health -= amount * 2 [/codeblock] [b]Copying, not inheriting:[/b] When a class uses a trait, the trait's members are copied into that class. This is what separates a trait from a base class: every class that uses the trait gets its own copy of its variables, so two classes using the same trait do not share state. A trait is not in the inheritance chain, so it has no parent and no children of its own. [b]Traits are not base types:[/b] A trait cannot be instantiated, and [code]extends SomeTrait[/code] is an error. To use a trait, declare it and then [code]uses[/code] it from a class. A class can [code]uses[/code] several traits, separated by commas. [b]Overriding members:[/b] A member declared on the class itself always wins over a trait member with the same name. Declaring a function with a trait's signature in the class overrides the trait's implementation, which is how a trait can offer a default that a class customizes. [b]Errors:[/b] A trait cannot contain inner classes or other traits. Using the same trait more than once in one class is an error. Calling a trait's functions directly, through a trait reference rather than an instance, is an error, because a trait has no instance of its own — call them on a class that uses it. [b]Note:[/b] Traits can only be declared and used within the same script file. Referencing a trait from another file, declaring a trait with [code]trait_name[/code], and testing a trait with [code]is[/code] or [code]as[/code] are not supported yet.
